results.flow_input_to_sink: Caller-supplied recipient `to` is passed from inherited ERC-721 transfer entrypoints into `Raffle._update(to, ticketId, auth)`, screened by `_isProtocolDestination(to, address(prizeToken))` (including external staticcalls to `RaffleFactory.raffleImplementation()` and, when `to.code.length != 0`, `RaffleFactory.isRaffle(to)`), and reaches `revert UnsafeProtocolDestination(to)`.
results.flow_security_relevance: Prevents bearer raffle tickets—which represent claims on the escrowed prize NFT, cash winner proceeds, or USDC refunds—from being transferred into protocol contracts (`Raffle`, `RaffleFactory`, `quoteToken`, `i_vrfV2PlusWrapper`, `prizeToken`, `raffleImplementation`, or registered sibling `Raffle` clones) where the ticket could never be redeemed or refunded. Deserves security review to verify completeness of the protocol sink denylist (e.g., whether `protocolTreasury` or `sponsorRecipient` contracts or unregistered addresses could still strand claims) and external staticcall behavior before authorization checks.
results.flow_summary: When a ticket owner or approved operator transfers a ticket to a non-zero address `to` that matches a known protocol contract or a registered raffle clone in `RaffleFactory`, `Raffle._update` detects the prohibited destination via `_isProtocolDestination` and reverts with `UnsafeProtocolDestination(to)` before modifying ERC-721 ownership.

results.flow_input_to_sink: Caller-controlled `to`, `ticketId`, and `auth` (`_msgSender()`) pass `_isProtocolDestination` screening and reach `super._update(to, ticketId, auth)`, which verifies `auth` against `ticketId` ownership/approvals, updates `_owners[ticketId]` and `_balances`, and (when called via `safeTransferFrom` to a contract `to`) triggers `IERC721Receiver(to).onERC721Received`.
results.flow_security_relevance: Mutates ERC-721 ticket ownership in any raffle lifecycle status (`Active`, `Drawing`, `NftWon`, `CashWon`, `Refunding`), including after `settleWinningTicket` has already locked `winningTicketId`. Because `redeemWinningTicket` and `refundTickets` authorize claims solely via `ownerOf(ticketId)` at claim time, transferring `ticketId` transfers the underlying NFT prize, cash payout, or refund entitlement. Additionally, inherited `transferFrom`/`safeTransferFrom` functions are not marked `nonReentrant`, so `safeTransferFrom` invokes `to.onERC721Received` after ownership mutation without setting `ReentrancyGuard`.
results.flow_summary: When a ticket owner or approved operator transfers a live ticket to a non-zero address `to` that is not flagged by `_isProtocolDestination`, `Raffle._update` delegates to `ERC721._update(to, ticketId, auth)`, verifying authorization, clearing prior token approvals, updating balances and `_owners[ticketId] = to`, emitting `Transfer`, and returning `previousOwner` (followed by `onERC721Received` if invoked via `safeTransferFrom` to a contract).
results.flow_terminal_action: Updates ERC-721 ownership and balances via `super._update(to, ticketId, auth)` at `packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol:501` and returns `previousOwner` (with subsequent `IERC721Receiver(to).onERC721Received` callback if invoked via `safeTransferFrom` to a contract recipient).

results.flow_security_relevance: Enforces the ERC-721 authorization boundary and prevents transferring nonexistent or already-burned tickets. Because `Raffle._ticketRanges[ticketId]` persists historically after `_burn(ticketId)` in `redeemWinningTicket` and `refundTickets`, `super._update` rejecting burned tokens (`owner == address(0)`) is critical to ensuring burned tickets cannot be transferred or resurrected.
